title: Experiment Automation Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Instrument interfaces, protocol definitions, run logs, and safety checks for automated experiments. The Experiment Automation Database documents experiments run by machines: instrument interfaces (how software talks to hardware), protocol definitions (the exact steps, machine-readable), run logs (everything that happened, timestamped), and safety checks (what must never happen, enforced). Automated experiments run faster and more reproducibly than manual ones — but only when the protocol is exact and the safety interlocks are real. Each record is a complete, re-runnable experimental protocol.

title: Experiment Automation Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Protocol anatomy: steps (action, target instrument, parameters, timeout, expected outcome), branches (if reading X then do Y), loops (repeat until condition), aborts (conditions that halt everything safely). Instrument interfaces: command sets, response formats, error codes, connection methods (serial, USB, TCP, GPIB); every command needs a timeout and an error path. Run logs: append-only, timestamped, include commands sent, responses, sensor readings, operator overrides. Safety: interlocks (hardware + software), limits (parameter bounds enforced before execution), abort conditions (checked every cycle), tested aborts (drilled, not assumed). Calibration: instruments calibrated on schedule; calibration records attached to run logs. Reproducibility: protocol version + instrument versions + reagent lots = the full context.

title: Experiment Automation Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: protocol test (every step has parameters and timeouts); safety test (missing interlocks flagged); interface test (commands valid per spec); replay test (logs replay deterministically). Limitations: demos simulate instruments; real automation needs hardware testing; safety review by qualified humans is mandatory. Every protocol carries version and calibration requirements.

demo.title: Verification: trade-off scoring and sensitivity
demo.code: const opts={A:{perf:9,rel:6,simple:5},B:{perf:6,rel:9,simple:8}};const w={perf:0.5,rel:0.3,simple:0.2};function score(o){return o.perf*w.perf+o.rel*w.rel+o.simple*w.simple;}const sA=score(opts.A),sB=score(opts.B);const w2={perf:0.3,rel:0.5,simple:0.2};function score2(o){return o.perf*w2.perf+o.rel*w2.rel+o.simple*w2.simple;}const flip=score2(opts.B)>score2(opts.A);J({sA:+sA.toFixed(2),sB:+sB.toFixed(2),flip});assert(sA>sB&&flip,'tradeoff');
